thread:
alice_support: FYI — Acme reported 429s from their dedicated pool after last night's policy rollout. Started ~2026-03-17T10:22:00Z. Error rate jumped and stayed high for ~6m. They see X-RateLimit-Remaining: 0 on responses.

ben_oncall: @alice_support could you paste the headers and a sample request/response? I want to see which rate key fired.

alice_support: sending clipped logs:
```
GET /v1/generate
Host: api.redwood.example
Authorization: Bearer sk-acme-xxx
X-Request-ID: req_01
Response: 429 Too Many Requests
Headers: X-RateLimit-Limit: 3600
X-RateLimit-Remaining: 0
X-RateLimit-Reset: 1618112400
```

emily_custsuccess: Customer says traffic pattern didn't change — they migrated a few tenants to reserved pool but normal traffic. They are upset, asking for immediate mitigation.

ben_oncall: autoscale-bot shows no infra OOMs, but there was a policy-rollout event at 10:20:13. @autoscale-bot can you dump the last 30s of decision log?

autoscale-bot: Decision log (trim): rollout policy v2 applied to pool-dedicated-42 at 2026-03-17T10:20:13Z; scale target unchanged; per-tenant-rate-override applied for plan "growth" -> units: 3600 (denom: HOURS)

carmen_eng: wait — denom: HOURS? the service expects units in MINUTES for this code path. we recently changed the UI to show hours but didn't convert in the backend when applying overrides. that would make a 1-hr quota appear as 3600/min which is 60x larger -> but reversed math can also undercount if the conversion path is opposite. need to confirm.

dave_sre: quick check: show me tenant config for acme-prod-tenant-17.

alice_support: config dump: "rate_units": "3600", "rate_denom": "HOURS", "applied_to_pool": "dedicated-42", "effective_rpu": 60

carmen_eng: looks like we double-converted: front-end stored hours, rate-service assumed minutes -> the final effective units dropped by factor of 60, so their per-tenant limit became ~1/60th of intended. that matches sudden 429s.

ben_oncall: mitigation proposals?

dave_sre: temp mitigation: apply tenant-override bypass for acme-prod-tenant-17 to high value while we patch conversion. I can do that in 5m. also route their keys to fallback pool in another region as short-term.

emily_custsuccess: i'll ask Acme if fallback routing is ok, they prefer no region change but acceptable for 30m. keep me posted so i can message them.

carmen_eng: i'll prepare a hotfix for rate-service to normalize denom on apply + add a unit test. patch -> canary -> prod today. estimated 60m to get hotfix in prod if no regressions.

ben_oncall: sounds good. action list: 1) @dave_sre apply tenant override to remove throttling now. 2) @carmen_eng ship denom-normalize hotfix and monitor. 3) @emily_custsuccess coordinate with customer re: fallback route if needed. 4) postmortem to follow.

dave_sre: applied override (temporary-override-618112): new headers now show X-RateLimit-Remaining: 3589, response 200. routing to fallback not needed for now. :white_check_mark:

carmen_eng: opened PR #4821 with fix + unit + integration test. kicking canary. deploy-bot: canary deploy scheduled.

deploy-bot: Canary deploy started for rate-service revision 2.14.3-canary at 2026-03-17T10:37:00Z. Health checks green.

alice_support: customer confirmed latency and errors cleared. They want root cause and permanent fix ETA.

ben_oncall: assigning owners: carmen_eng (fix) + dave_sre (mitigation + rollback if needed) + alice_support/emily_custsuccess for customer comms. I'll file incident and link this thread.

carmen_eng: postmortem plan: include timeline, code diff, why unit tests missed it, and add an audit check to verify denom alignment on rollout. pulling logs now.

alice_support: thanks all, leaving notes for follow-ups and tagging for SLA. :pray:
